newsitem.title: CANADA: India assets good example of target - Gulf.
newsitem.headline: India assets good example of target - Gulf.

text.p: Oil and gas assets in India, like those Gulf Canada Resources Ltd looked at recently by considering a rival bid for Australia's Command Petroleum Holdings NL, are a good example of the kind of acquisition Gulf is targeting, a company spokesman said on Thursday.

Gulf Canada's John Sparks confirmed a Reuters report Thursday that the company and Hardy Oil & Gas Plc conducted due diligence to see if they could launch a higher bid for Command, the target of a A$354.5 million (C$368.7 million) bid from Cairn Energy Plc.

However, Gulf's acquisition team determined Cairn's A$1.10 (C$1.14) per share offer for the company "was fully valued," which prevented a sweetened offer, Sparks said. Gulf has since moved on to examine other opportunities.

Gulf chief executive J.P. Bryan has said several times that the company is scouring the globe for another international acquisition to complement its operations in Indonesia, where it is a partner in the Corridor Block natural gas project.

"The Indian situation is very similar to the (Production Sharing Contract) arrangements we've worked with in Indonesia for a long time, in terms of the cost recovery and the way they're structured," he said.
"It is certainly the kind of asset (Gulf is examining), when we talk about putting a third leg on the stool."
He said the company, which is also a large producer in Canada, would move quickly when an acquisition target was identified. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
